title: How many zero pairs let five positives leave three negatives?
description: Three negative tokens sit on a tray and five positive tokens must be taken away. Zero pairs are put in until five positive tokens can be lifted off, and the tokens that stay give the result.
teaching_notes: One idea: put in one zero pair for each positive token to take away, then lift the positive tokens off. Watch for students who take three from five and get a small positive answer.

video_script.why: The child subtracts positive tokens from negative tokens by putting in zero pairs, and counts how many are needed.
video_script.substitution: Put in one zero pair for each positive token to take away, lift off the positive tokens, and read the result from the tokens that stay.
video_script.payoff_line: We put in five zero pairs, and the result is negative eight.

final_answer.value: Five zero pairs; the result is −8.
final_answer.spoken: five zero pairs, and the result is negative eight

maths_rules: (−3) is 3 negative tokens; 5 positive tokens must be taken out, but none are on the tray
each zero pair holds 1 positive token, so 5 zero pairs give 5 positive tokens; the value stays −3
the tray now holds 3 + 5 = 8 negative tokens and 5 positive tokens
take out the 5 positive tokens: 8 negative tokens stay, so (−3) − (+5) = −8
check: 8 negative and 5 positive tokens, less 5 zero pairs = 3 negative tokens
video_script.design: One tray of three negative tokens. Five zero pairs are put in, the five positive tokens are lifted off, and eight negative tokens stay.
